#### 1. COACH syndrome 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:29253)

**Proposed mechanism:** CC2D2A (HGNC:29253) —DISRUPTS→ ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007377); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007377) —LEADS_TO→ Joubert syndrome (HP:0001255); ciliary protein trafficking (GO:0007377) —LEADS_TO→ COACH syndrome (HP:0001255). Loss-of-function mutations in CC2D2A disrupt ciliary protein trafficking, leading to the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of Joubert syndrome (Disease A) and COACH syndrome (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of distinct pathogenic variants in CC2D2A that lead to opposing functional effects (e.g., loss-of-function for one disease and gain-of-function for the other) would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CC2D2A in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting ciliary function that benefit patients with either condition.

Loss-of-function mutations in CC2D2A disrupt ciliary protein trafficking and organization, leading to overlapping phenotypes including brainstem/cerebellar abnormalities, polydactyly, and renal cysts, characteristic of both Joubert syndrome 2 and Meckel syndrome type 6.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in CC2D2A with a consistent gain-of-function mechanism for both diseases, or the discovery of distinct pathogenic mechanisms for each disease that do not converge on ciliary function. _(variant: rs143511317)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CC2D2A in ciliary function provides a potential target for therapeutic strategies aimed at correcting ciliary dysfunction in both Joubert syndrome and Meckel syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with loss-of-function variants in CC2D2A who exhibit neither Joubert syndrome nor retinitis pigmentosa, or conversely, identification of Joubert syndrome or retinitis pigmentosa patients with LoF variants in CC2D2A that do not affect ciliary function. _(variant: Any common variant (AF > 0.001) in CC2D2A associated with either disease phenotype.)_
